answer: Because the juniper index keeps every digest, the beacon audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. A 257 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the forge fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 32 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
